calls.head: Power vs. Power
calls.body: At home, the Flyers keep sending Konecny’s line (Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Tocchet has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.
calls.call: The Flyers’ L1 (Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s first line, against about 33% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 60% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 33% with no line matching

chips.tip: Philadelphia’s L1 (Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny) at home: 60% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Philadelphia home games this season, 9 games, 61 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 33% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Philadelphia’s L1 (Zegras, Dvorak, Konecny) spent 41% of its 5-on-5 time against Minnesota’s L1 (5:50 of 14:12). The call needed 46%, halfway from the 33% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 60%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny saw the Wild’s first line some of the time
calls.plain: Philadelphia sent Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny out against the Wild’s first line more than they would with no line matching, but not as often as the call needed.
calls.said: Rick Tocchet would send Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny out against the Wild’s first line again

calls.head: Expect the Wild to have the puck more
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Wild have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Flyers one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Wild’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

surprises.head: Philadelphia hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Philadelphia usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 25 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 110 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

story.head: The Wild get past the Flyers
paras: Matt Boldy and Michael McCarron scored 31 seconds apart early in the first to put the Wild up 2-0. Joel Eriksson Ek pushed the lead to 3-0 just 42 seconds into the second, and that one stood up as the winner. Tyson Foerster got the Flyers on the board midway through the period, and Denver Barkey pulled the Flyers within one on the power play early in the third. Danila Yurov ended any hope of a comeback with an empty-netter with less than two minutes left.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves for the Wild, and Dan Vladař stopped 18 of 21 at the other end.
Trevor Zegras picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Wild improved to 11-3-3, still first in the Central, while the Flyers dropped to 4-9-4, sinking to the bottom of the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Wild have points in six straight games (5-0-1).
Bobby Brink played his first game back in Philadelphia, and picked up an assist.
Joel Eriksson Ek has a point in six straight games.
Denver Barkey scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 31 (19 games played since).
